summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with a flare of chronic pancreatitis, presenting with epigastric pain radiating to the back, nausea, vomiting, and inability to tolerate oral intake. She also reported dysuria and was found to have a urinary tract infection caused by E. coli, which was treated with ciprofloxacin. Her pain was managed with IV fluids and a transition from IV to oral analgesics, including tramadol, while avoiding narcotics. Blood pressure was elevated during stress and pain episodes, leading to an increase in lisinopril from 10 mg to 30 mg daily. She remained on levetiracetam for seizure prevention, with plans to transition to lamictal. The patient improved over the course of admission, tolerated oral intake, and was discharged home with services after demonstrating stability on her outpatient medication regimen. Follow-up was arranged with her PCP, neurology, and a partial psychiatric program she had previously missed due to hospitalization.
